findings.finding: Item 3 (target repo) handles `--git-dir` by exporting `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` for the hook's own git calls, but doesn't state what directory is used for manifest/config/spec lookups in that case. With `--git-dir` alone (no `--work-tree`), git treats the cwd as the work tree — but the plan's `target_root` appears to derive a root from the `--git-dir` path, which is typically `.git`'s parent or even a bare location, not the project the commit belongs to.
findings.suggestion: Define lookups explicitly: `--work-tree` if given, else cwd when only `--git-dir` is given, else the accumulated `-C` path. Also decide what happens when `-C <path>` points at a subdirectory of a repo whose manifest lives at the repo root — walking up to find the manifest (or at least documenting that `-C` must name the project root) avoids a confusing "manifest not found" WARN.

findings.finding: The override helper parses a free-text log written by the agent, and `instruction()` prints a `printf ... >> log` line the agent copies verbatim. If the reason (or hook-generated default) contains quotes, `%`, or newline/ANSI sequences, the printf line breaks or the WARN echoing the reason becomes a terminal-escape injection vector. The log is also inside the repo, so it can end up committed with entries whose reason text is later rendered by hooks.
findings.suggestion: Have `instruction()` emit the reason shell-quoted (`shlex.quote`) or use a fixed canonical reason string; strip control characters from reasons when parsing/echoing, and note in docs that the log should be gitignored (or add it to the ignore list in this change).

findings.finding: The 30-minute window check tolerates 1 minute of future skew but the plan doesn't state the behavior for an unparseable/malformed log line. A single bad line (agent typo, since the agent hand-writes the line) shouldn't disable override functionality or crash the hook.
findings.suggestion: Specify "skip unparseable lines silently" (or with a debug note) in the helper and cover it with one test.

findings.finding: Item 1 changes `compute_coverage`'s output contract (new `fr.not_measured` key, requirements leaving the figures). Any other consumer of the manifest-coverage figures (reports, docs reconcile in U12) may read the old shape. The plan updates tests but doesn't inventory other callers.
findings.suggestion: Grep for callers of `compute_coverage`/`measure` output keys and confirm none breaks on the new field; note it explicitly for U12 since that unit is next and docs-reconciles.

findings.finding: Heredoc stripping: the plan handles quoted/unquoted delimiters and keeps `$(...)` in unquoted bodies, but doesn't mention `<<-EOF` tab-stripped terminators with trailing tabs, or a heredoc whose terminator never appears (truncated/interactive command). A missing terminator that swallows the rest of the command buffer could hide a real `git commit`.
findings.suggestion: For a missing terminator, treat the remainder as inside the heredoc (strip it) or not stripped — either is defensible; pick one, document it, and test the truncated case so behavior is pinned.

findings.finding: New single-purpose modules `lib/compliance_override.py`, `lib/git_commit_target.py`, `lib/shell_heredoc.py` each exist to keep files under the 300-line cap. That's fine and per the acceptance criteria ("extract rather than grow"), but `git_commit_target` duplicating option-parsing that `find_git_commit` already does (returning global options) risks the two parsers drifting.
findings.suggestion: Have `find_git_commit` return the structured global options and make `git_commit_target` a pure consumer of that structure — the mini-plan implies this, but make it explicit so the parsing logic exists once.

findings.finding: The override authorizes every matching hook invocation for 30 minutes, while the binding decision authorizes the next commit within that window. The alternative explicitly rejects single-use behavior, so this needs resolution before implementation.
findings.suggestion: Implement a shared mechanism that claims the override for one commit attempt, with a defined retry policy for failed commits. If repeated authorization is intended, obtain and record an amended operator decision.

findings.finding: Resolving only the first commit leaves compound commands unhandled. For example, `git -C repoA commit && git -C repoB commit` could check repo A’s evidence while also allowing a commit to repo B. Falling back to cwd when a target cannot be resolved likewise checks unrelated evidence.
findings.suggestion: Resolve and evaluate every detected commit target. If a target cannot be resolved, report that explicitly and require the established override instead of treating cwd coverage as valid evidence. Add real-repo tests for compound commands and unresolved targets.

findings.finding: Keeping an entire heredoc line whenever it contains `$(` or a backtick reintroduces false positives. An unquoted heredoc containing `Example: git commit $(date)` executes `date`, but does not execute `git commit`.
findings.suggestion: Scan only executable command-substitution contents from unquoted heredocs. Test literal commit text beside an unrelated substitution, an actual commit inside a substitution, quoted delimiters, and tab-stripped terminators.

findings.finding: The mini-plan omits two explicit acceptance deliverables: recording decisions 1 and 2 in the U13 decision drop, and closing the U9 triage card with its ID in the PR body.
findings.suggestion: Add both to the completion checklist, and verify the under-300-line limit for every touched file, including tests.  The coverage exclusion and heading-depth changes are sound and appropriately scoped. The override semantics and commit-target handling need specific corrections before this approach meets the specification.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
